title: Earwax removal
what: An ENT doctor removes built-up earwax. The ear is rinsed with warm water, or the wax is taken out with a small tool.
why: When your ear feels blocked, your hearing drops, or it feels muffled after swimming, and the doctor sees a wax plug.
tell_doctor: If you have had a hole in your eardrum or ear surgery
If your ear has leaked fluid, hurt, or you had a fever
If you use a hearing aid

prepare.title: Softening
prepare.text: Sometimes the doctor asks you to use ear drops for a few days to soften the wax. Do only what the doctor said.

prepare.title: Hands off
prepare.text: Do not use cotton swabs in your ear. They push the wax deeper.

bring: Your referral, if you have one
Your hearing aid, if you wear one
steps: The doctor looks into your ear with a small funnel or a camera
If the eardrum is intact, the ear is rinsed with warm water from a syringe with no needle
The water and wax drain into a small tray held at your neck
Sometimes the wax is removed with a tool or gentle suction
The doctor looks again and checks your eardrum
feel: Warm water in your ear, with noise and gurgling
You may feel a little dizzy. Tell the doctor
Right after, your hearing usually comes back
after: You can wipe the outside of your ear, but do not put swabs inside
If this happens often, ask your doctor how to prevent wax plugs
red_flags: Severe ear pain, or blood or pus from the ear after the procedure
Sudden hearing loss or severe dizziness

faq.q: Can I remove earwax at home?
faq.a: Do not use swabs or hairpins. You can damage your eardrum. If your ear feels blocked, see an ENT doctor.
Usually not. It feels warm, noisy, and a bit strange.
